title: Excel Pivot Table & Dashboard from Scratch
description: Build a complete pivot table and dashboard using sample sales data
objective: Students will create a dataset, build pivot tables to answer business questions, create charts, and assemble a professional dashboard in Excel

steps.title: Create the Dataset
steps.instructions:
Open Excel and create a new workbook. Name Sheet1 as **"Sales Data"**.

Create these column headers in Row 1:
`Date | Salesperson | Region | Product | Units | Price | Revenue`

Enter at least 40 rows of data. Use these values:
- **Dates:** Jan 2026 to Mar 2026 (mix of dates)
- **Salesperson:** Rahul, Priya, Amit, Sneha
- **Region:** North, South, West
- **Product:** Laptop, Mouse, Keyboard, Monitor, Headphones
- **Units:** Random numbers 1-20
- **Price:** Laptop=45000, Mouse=500, Keyboard=1200, Monitor=12000, Headphones=2000
- **Revenue:** Formula `=E2*F2` (drag down for all rows)

Format the Revenue column as Currency (₹).
Format the Date column as DD-MMM-YYYY.

steps.title: Build the Pivot Table
steps.instructions:
Select your entire data range (Ctrl+A on the data).

Go to **Insert → PivotTable → New Worksheet**.

Rename the new sheet as **"Analysis"**.

**Pivot Table 1 — Revenue by Salesperson:**
- Drag **Salesperson** to Rows
- Drag **Revenue** to Values (should show Sum)

**Pivot Table 2 — Monthly Revenue by Region:**
- Create a new PivotTable on the same sheet
- Drag **Date** to Rows → right-click → Group → Months
- Drag **Region** to Columns
- Drag **Revenue** to Values

**Pivot Table 3 — Product Performance:**
- Create a third PivotTable
- Drag **Product** to Rows
- Drag **Units** to Values (Sum)
- Drag **Revenue** to Values (Sum)
- Sort by Revenue descending

steps.title: Add Slicers for Interactive Filtering
steps.instructions:
Click on Pivot Table 1. Go to **PivotTable Analyze → Insert Slicer**.

Check: **Region** and **Product** → OK.

Two slicer panels appear. Click "North" in the Region slicer — watch the pivot table filter instantly!

Hold Ctrl and click multiple items to multi-select.

To connect a slicer to multiple pivot tables:
- Right-click the slicer → **Report Connections**
- Check all three PivotTables

Now clicking one slicer filters ALL pivot tables simultaneously.

steps.title: Create Charts
steps.instructions:
Click on Pivot Table 1 → **Insert → Chart**:
- Choose **Bar Chart** → Title: "Revenue by Salesperson"
- Add data labels (click chart → + icon → Data Labels)

Click on Pivot Table 2 → **Insert → Chart**:
- Choose **Line Chart** → Title: "Monthly Revenue Trend"
- Each region becomes a separate line

Click on Pivot Table 3 → **Insert → Chart**:
- Choose **Pie Chart** for Revenue → Title: "Revenue by Product"
- Show percentages (Format Data Labels → check Percentage)

Format all charts:
- Remove chart borders
- Use consistent colors
- Make fonts readable (12pt+)

steps.title: Assemble the Dashboard
steps.instructions:
Create a new sheet → name it **"Dashboard"**.

1. Add a title row: **"Sales Dashboard — Q1 2026"** (Merge & Center, bold, 18pt)

2. Add KPI boxes at the top using cells:
   - Total Revenue: `=SUM('Sales Data'!G:G)` formatted as ₹
   - Total Units: `=SUM('Sales Data'!E:E)`
   - Average Order: `=AVERAGE('Sales Data'!G:G)` formatted as ₹
   - Top Salesperson: `=INDEX('Sales Data'!B:B,MATCH(MAX('Sales Data'!G:G),'Sales Data'!G:G,0))`

3. Move your 3 charts to this sheet (right-click chart → Move Chart → Dashboard sheet)

4. Move slicers to the dashboard

5. Arrange everything neatly:
   - KPIs at top
   - Bar chart and line chart side by side
   - Pie chart and slicers below

6. Remove gridlines: View → uncheck Gridlines

7. Add a light background color to the KPI cells

**Screenshot your finished dashboard and submit the Excel file.**

expected_output: An Excel workbook with 4 sheets: Sales Data (40+ rows), Analysis (3 pivot tables), charts, and a formatted Dashboard sheet with KPIs, charts, and interactive slicers
